现状与痛点

你的才华，不该耗在台账和聊天记录里

开工作室是因为热爱创作与教学。没有人是为了对账、催费、翻聊天记录才创业的。

被打断的排练

「还剩几节课？」一句询问，要翻三个月的群记录才答得上。

深夜的对账表

白天上课，晚上核 Excel，吃掉的是备课和新作品的时间。

经不起丢的纸条

收据在抽屉、承诺在口头，家长的信任不该系在一张纸上。

看不见的作品墙

作品攒了一屋子，线上无处可看，新学员只能靠转介绍。

台前是你的品牌，幕后是一个系统

四个界面，同一个工作室在其中流动

台前始终是你的品牌，背后流动的是同一套事实——从第一次访问走到每天上课，不再是四套断开的工具，也不再共用一个权限过大的账号。

品牌工作台
01
一扇打开就像你工作室的门

门户用你的身份呈现课程、精选作品与常见问题。家庭可以先了解工作室、不离开页面直接报名，之后再从学员区回来。

已发布品牌 → 课程 → 作品 → 学员区
访问工作室门户
02
每一次意向，都带着完整来路抵达

快速报名可以放在二维码或推广链接后面，使用工作室自己的问题，与门户进入同一条审核队列，并保留来源与语言。

二维码或推广 → 同一字段 → 同一审核队列
开始一次报名
03
把工作室的一天真正跑完的地方

运营 CMS 把学员、排课、签到、课时、收款、报名跟进、作品与报表接在一起。每个角色只看到自己真正能完成的工作。

店主 · 店长 · 老师 · 前台 · 助教
进入运营 CMS
04
品牌可以改变，不必每次都找开发者

品牌工作台管理 Logo、配色、双语文案、公开版块与报名字段。先预览草稿，再明确发布，也能回到一个已知版本。

草稿 → 预览 → 发布 → 恢复
进入品牌工作台
05

四个界面之外，另有平台侧 Super Admin：租户开通、套餐与账单、用量监控、审计日志。平台方不持有工作室账号，也不读取学员资料；进店必须走留痕的支持模式。

行业模版

行业模版换的是术语和表单，不只是颜色。
美术工作室

作品成长、发布授权、学期课程与材料导向的课程叙事。

音乐学校

乐器、级别、练习目标、课程节奏与演出里程碑。

舞蹈工作室

舞种、级别、课表、出勤与排练沟通。

补习机构

科目、年级、学习目标、课时与进度证据。

创意科技

项目、工作坊、编程路径与可分享成果。

三个关键设计

钱和信任，写进系统，不写在人情里

下面三件事没有一件是功能清单上的卖点，它们是决定这套系统能不能被托付的地方。

账本不可篡改

余额 = 每一笔流水之和。不是一个可以随手改掉的数字，每次变动都记录操作人、时间与原因。签到自动扣课时，余额不足当场拦截并提醒。

权限写死在后端

店主 / 店长 / 老师 / 前台 / 员工，五级权限。前台能收费不能退费，退费与对外分享仅限店主店长，不是在界面上藏起来，是系统层面直接拒绝——把人情压力从员工身上移到系统上。

未成年人隐私

两百多项租户隔离测试每次发版全绿才允许上线；作品公开须记录监护人同意，同意与撤回是只增不改的事件链；分享链接 1–90 天强制到期，可随时撤销。

text:
跳到主要内容

Caulfield North, Melbourne VIC

颜色会把人放慢下来。

墨尔本 Caulfield North 的一间小画室。成人小班，一次不超过八个人，从握笔开始也来得及。

预约体验
看看作品
学员登录 →
LET'S PAINT STUDIO

这里不赶进度，也不比谁画得快。每周两小时，或者只来一次看看合不合适，都可以。

空间

一间朝南的后院画室

画室在一栋 1920 年代砖房的后院，原本是马厩改的车库，屋顶掀高了，南墙换成一整面玻璃。我们没有装射灯——南边的光一整天不变色，这是画画的人唯一挑不出毛病的光。 门口有两棵梧桐，风大的时候能听见。颜料、亚麻布、画架、围裙都在，你带一件不怕脏的衣服就行。

LET'S PAINT STUDIO

Nothing here is a race. Two hours a week, or one afternoon to see whether it suits you — both are a reasonable way to start.

THE ROOM

A garden studio facing south

The studio is the old stable at the back of a 1920s brick house — the roof lifted, the south wall replaced with glass. We didn't put in spotlights: south light doesn't change colour all day, which is the only light a painter never argues with. Two plane trees by the gate, loud in a westerly. Paint, linen, easels and aprons are here. Bring a shirt you don't mind ruining.

01
Eight easels, and no ninth

Eight is a ceiling, not a target. In two hours the teacher can stand behind each person three times, which is the only thing a small class is really for.

02
The materials are ours

Oils, linen, solvent and aprons belong to the studio. Come once and buy nothing — there is no list to ask about.

03
Wet canvases stay

Oil takes its time and there is a shelf with your name on it. Nobody has to finish a painting because it is half past eight.

Janet M

FOUNDER & PRINCIPAL

Janet M

Janet studied painting in Beijing and spent eight years in advertising after moving to Melbourne. In 2019 she cleared out the old stable behind a house in Caulfield North, painted it white and put in eight easels — at first only so she would have somewhere to paint, then because a neighbour knocked and asked to join her. Her classes have no syllabus and no ranking. The first one usually happens on the palette: work out what colour the grey in front of you actually is, and the rest follows.

The grey you're looking at is never grey.

Find your rhythm. Make every practice count.

A teaching studio in Glen Waverley, Melbourne. Piano, violin and voice; guzheng, erhu and pipa. One-on-one lessons, groups of four to six, and an ensemble that rehearses on Saturday afternoons.

ZHIYIN MUSIC

The first lesson is mostly playing and listening, so everyone can see whether this fits. If it doesn't, say so — nobody has to commit to a term first.

THE ROOMS

Four rooms, and one that fits the whole ensemble

The studio is a 1970s brick house on a side street in Glen Waverley — six minutes from the station, two hours' free parking at the door. The front of the house is divided into four teaching rooms with rockwool in the walls and seals on the doors, so an erhu next door does not turn up in a piano lesson. The largest room holds a dozen people and the grand piano, and belongs to the ensemble on Saturday afternoons. There are two sofas in the front room for waiting parents, and you are welcome in for the last ten minutes of any lesson.

01
The soundproofing is in the walls

The four teaching rooms were rebuilt with insulated stud walls and sealed doors. An erhu lesson and a piano lesson can run at the same time without either being in the other's way — less a renovation detail than the reason a timetable is possible at all.

02
Two pianos, tuned twice a year

An upright in Studio 1 and a grand in the big room — the two that get tuned — where exam run-throughs and the June concert happen. Studio 2 has a digital piano for the early-years group. Five guzheng in the guzheng room, restrung once a term, plus a practice erhu and a practice pipa.

03
Somewhere for parents to wait

Two sofas, wifi, and coffee ten minutes' walk away. In the last ten minutes of each lesson the teacher goes through the week's practice points with the parent in the room — not a report, just so whoever supervises practice has heard it too.

04
Lessons in English or Mandarin

Most teachers work in either language; say which you would prefer when you enrol. Lesson notes and the end-of-term report are written in both, which covers the school and the grandparents at once.

05
Saturday afternoons are the ensemble

Eight to twelve players, Chinese and Western instruments in the same room. A year of lessons is the only way in — no grade required. They play twice a year: June in the studio, December in a community hall.

06
The exam dates are on the wall

AMEB session dates and entry deadlines go up in the front room, and we book the run-through slots as a studio. VCE students play their whole program in the big room once a term — not marked, just so the standing-up part has already happened once.

Vivian H

FOUNDER & PRINCIPAL TEACHER

Vivian H

Vivian started guzheng in Shanghai at six, came to Melbourne with her family at fourteen and carried on here on piano, stopping after Grade 8. She studied accounting, spent six years at a firm, and taught two or three students every weekend throughout — for a while she could not have told you which was the job. In 2020 she took the lease on the Glen Waverley house and divided the front rooms into four studios. The name comes from zhiyin, the listener who hears what you meant: in the old story Boya plays and Zhong Ziqi hears the mountain and the river in it. Most of teaching, she says, is that — work out what the student is actually playing, then say what comes next.

Practise one phrase until you want to play it again — that is the day done.

What gets played here

Term concerts, exam programs, and whatever the ensemble is working on. Where there is a recording we publish it; where there is not, a photograph. We never publish a recording nobody agreed to.

风过果园

布面油画与炭笔，90 × 90 cm，2025。风停之后那半小时，树还没缓过来。

陶罐与柠檬

布面油画，60 × 60 cm，2025。柠檬是课上剩下的，摆了一周才画。

港口的形状

布面油画，刮刀，75 × 75 cm，2024。桅杆先画，剩下的都是为了托住它们。

月下荚果

布面丙烯与油彩，80 × 80 cm，2025。夜里画的，第二天看颜色全对，很少这样。

南岸，三点钟

布面油画，刮刀，60 × 60 cm，2024。风大的那种下午，海是灰绿的，草是热的。

金色的田

布面油画，70 × 70 cm，2024。开车去 Castlemaine 的路上，停了二十分钟。

海边的枝叶

布面油画与拼贴，70 × 70 cm，2025。近处的叶子和远处的海，是同一种蓝。

高草与河

布面油画，65 × 65 cm，2024。草比水难画，因为草会动。

无花果树与潮水

布面油画，70 × 70 cm，2025。院子里的树，背后是想象的海。

一枚红荚

纸本油彩，50 × 50 cm，2025。一节课的时间，一个东西。

退潮笔记

布面油画，60 × 60 cm，2024。退潮的沙滩有六种颜色，我只画得出四种。

金合欢与桉叶

水彩与水粉，40 × 40 cm，2025。窗台上放了三天的一把花，第二天开始掉，画的是第三天。

一间朝南的后院画室

画室在一栋 1920 年代砖房的后院，原本是马厩改的车库，屋顶掀高了，南墙换成一整面玻璃。我们没有装射灯——南边的光一整天不变色，这是画画的人唯一挑不出毛病的光。 门口有两棵梧桐，风大的时候能听见。颜料、亚麻布、画架、围裙都在，你带一件不怕脏的衣服就行。

Janet M

Janet 在北京学的画，来墨尔本之后做了八年广告。2019 年她把 Caulfield North 那栋房子后院的旧马厩收拾出来，刷成白色，摆了八张画架——最初只是想有个地方自己画画，后来邻居敲门问能不能一起。 她的课没有进度表，也不排名次。第一节课通常在调色盘上度过：先弄清楚你眼睛里的灰到底是什么颜色，剩下的都好说。
